central_question: By 31 December 2027, what are the probability-weighted global economic, macro-financial and geopolitical consequences of the Russia-Ukraine war, conditional on an explicitly defined war end-state (active high-intensity war, reduced-intensity attrition, frozen conflict, formal armistice, or comprehensive peace settlement), priced across Brent, TTF, gold, euro-area inflation and rates, and European defense spending?

situation_brief.current_situation: As of late October 2026, Russia holds about 19% of Ukraine (~45,196 sq miles incl. Crimea and pre-2022 Donbas) after a slow year of gains (+753 sq miles over 12 months), but momentum has reversed: Russia's four-week net gain fell to 3 sq miles, with Ukraine retaking 20 sq miles on Oct 13-19, and ISW assesses Russia's Donetsk offensive has been 'operationally defeated'. No ceasefire text exists. Talks collapsed in Geneva in February 2026; after the ninth Witkoff-Putin meeting, Russia agreed in principle to resume trilateral talks after November 10. Markets carry a double shock: Brent ~$115/b and TTF ~€92/MWh, driven largely by a Middle East energy disruption plus the war; gold averages $4,334/oz; euro-area HICP 3.8% with core 2.5%; ECB deposit rate 2.50% after two 2026 hikes; Fed upper limit 4% after a September hike.
situation_brief.context: The war is in its fifth year of full-scale fighting, well beyond the 2.1-year interstate average, with Iran-Iraq (8 years to ceasefire) the closest duration analog. Russia's fiscal strain is real (2026 deficit estimate 3.2% of GDP vs 1.6% target; 2027 borrowing up 43%; security 44% of 2027 spending) but not yet binding. Ukraine's binding constraint is manpower: 200,000 AWOL, 2 million evading draft notices, average soldier over 40. Europe leads military aid but depends on US weapons; Ukraine faces a ~€70 billion 2027 funding gap against €45 billion planned from the EU. US politics (diesel peaked at $6.53/gallon before the November 3 midterms) is driving unilateral, pre-deal US sanctions relief (diesel license to April 2027, Graham Act waiver, possible shadow-fleet relief) that diverges from the EU's ratcheting 20th sanctions package.
situation_brief.dynamics: The central obstacle is sequencing: Putin insists talks cover the security parameters of a final peace deal, 'not a short ceasefire', while Zelensky says Ukraine is ready to freeze the front line now and wants a ceasefire first plus security guarantees (NATO membership, US Article-5-style guarantees, or a European Coalition of the Willing). Trump is pressing Kyiv to deal and has linked the track to Russia helping on Iran. Ukraine's counteroffensive (Operation Vivaldi) has stabilised the front; drone output is scaling on both sides; Russian mobilization signals (convict contracts, regional staff cuts) have not become a decree. The probability mass sits on de-escalation without signature (frozen conflict 32% + reduced-intensity attrition 35%), with signed termination at 18% and active high-intensity war at 15%.
fault_lines: Ceasefire-first vs final-deal-first sequencing between Kyiv and Moscow
US unilateral pre-deal sanctions relief vs EU ratcheting 20th package and prospective maritime-services ban
Ukraine's manpower crisis (200,000 AWOL, 2 million evading notices) vs Russia's thinning but functional fiscal-military buffer
Security-guarantee architecture: Putin's red line on Western peacekeeping troops vs Ukraine's demand for guarantees
Ukraine's ~€70 billion 2027 funding gap vs €45 billion planned EU support and US dependence of European aid
Election-cycle fuel politics in the US (diesel peaked at $6.53/gallon) vs coalition sanctions discipline
catalysts: Trilateral Russia-Ukraine-US talks expected on/after November 10, 2026, possibly Abu Dhabi
EU summit on 2027 Ukraine financing, November 26-27, 2026
Expiry of US diesel-sanctions license, April 2027
FOMC October 27-28 and December 2026 meetings; ECB meetings from February 3-4, 2027
Russian mobilization decree or new nuclear exercise
OSINT confirmation of three months of near-zero front-line movement

key_events.event: First trilateral Russia-Ukraine-US round held in Abu Dhabi; no text produced.
Trilateral rounds in Abu Dhabi and Geneva ended in impasse with no text.
Former high-ranking Western official estimated Ukrainian casualties at 250,000-300,000 killed and wounded.
CSIS study estimated roughly 600,000 Ukrainians killed, wounded or missing.
UK estimate put Ukrainian casualties at 1,225,000 killed and wounded.
Ukrainian Defense Minister Fedorov estimated 200,000 soldiers absent without leave and 2 million men avoided draft notices.
Ukrainian reforms raised specialist pay and expanded foreign-volunteer recruitment.
Reported Russian nuclear signal package, including an exercise, correlated with battlefield setbacks.
Council adoption of SAFE instrument of up to €150 billion in EU-budget-backed loans.
ECB raised deposit facility rate to 2.25% (second 2026 hike after June; held 2.00% March-May).
NATO June 2026 release put 2026 defence spending of European Allies and Canada at around USD 634 billion, 2.53% of GDP.
Reports that Russia halted Kerch Strait commercial transits; unconfirmed.
Duma law allowed people with criminal convictions to sign military contracts during mobilization.
Rheinmetall delivered first Unterlüß 155mm rounds, targeting about 1.5 million a year by end-2026.
ECB raised all three key rates by 25bp; deposit facility to 2.50%, effective 16 September.
FOMC raised target range to 3-3/4 to 4 percent by a 12-0 vote.
Putin warned Europe of war if peacekeeping troops are deployed to Ukraine, per Washington Post report.
Weekly US diesel price peaked at $6.53/gallon.
Trump announced a Russian diesel purchase deal; Treasury license suspends US sanctions on Russian diesel deliveries until April 2027.
EU gas storage 74.0% full (836.9 TWh), lowest for the season since 2018.
Reuters reported the US administration is weighing lifting sanctions on some shadow-fleet vessels.
Trump signed an executive order waiving the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026.
Oslo meeting: US envoy Witkoff, Zelensky, Finland, Norway and European/NATO representatives; proposals tabled, no text.
Ninth in-person Witkoff-Putin meeting in St Petersburg, three hours; US citizen Stephen Hubbard released.
Zelensky said on Fox News Ukraine is ready to freeze the conflict along the current front line.
Russia agreed in principle to resume trilateral talks after November 10, possibly Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky named three unagreed postwar security-guarantee options: NATO membership, direct US guarantees, European Coalition of the Willing.
Putin stated Russia is ready for three-way talks on security parameters of a final peace deal, not a 'short' ceasefire.
Eurostat release: euro-area headline HICP 3.8% y/y for September 2026.
US midterm elections scheduled.
EU leaders to meet (26-27 November) on 2027 Ukraine financing; €45 billion planned against ~€70 billion gap.
Expiry of the US Treasury license suspending sanctions on Russian diesel deliveries.
US banned enriched-uranium imports from Russia (then ~$1 billion a year), with a legislated ban running to 2028.
MarketWatch quoted ICE Brent Dec-2027 futures at $81.98/bbl.

scenarios.name: Active high-intensity war
scenarios.narrative: Escalation dynamics, broken diplomacy and sustained Russian war-economy output keep full-scale fighting at or above late-2026 intensity through end-2027; prior: multi-year attritional interstate wars rarely terminate within 6 years of onset.

scenarios.name: Reduced-intensity attrition
scenarios.narrative: Both sides' manpower and munitions constraints plus election-cycle pressure in the West lower the tempo, but no durable deal holds and fighting continues into end-2027.

scenarios.name: Frozen conflict
scenarios.narrative: Zelensky's stated openness to freezing the frontline and partial-truce precedents produce a de facto ceasefire without a signed agreement; prior: frozen lines are the modal end-state of long interstate conflicts.

scenarios.name: Formal armistice
scenarios.narrative: Sustained US mediation and mutual exhaustion produce a signed ceasefire or armistice with a monitoring line in force before end-2027.

scenarios.name: Comprehensive peace settlement
scenarios.narrative: Only a political rupture in Moscow or a decisive battlefield outcome yields a signed comprehensive settlement in 2027; no framework text currently exists, so the base rate stays low.
